text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"Uses the article’s accident/liability question and safety limits of the cars","quality":"use of textual evidence","description":"The essay grounds its argument in several details from the source instead of relying mainly on general claims."},{"evidence":"Several linked paragraphs about internet failure, liability, and unfinished technology","quality":"argument development","description":"The essay develops multiple reasons against driverless cars and expands each one with explanation."},{"evidence":"“What happens if the internet fails while the car is in motion?” / “who is at fault?”","quality":"rhetorical questioning","description":"The essay uses questions effectively to press its point and keep the reader engaged."},{"evidence":"“For the saftey of our world…” / “Driverless cars are a completely bad idea.”","quality":"assertive stance","description":"The essay states a clear position and returns to it forcefully throughout the response."},{"evidence":"Conclusion restates the main reasons and warns about harm","quality":"conclusion strength","description":"The ending clearly summarizes the argument and leaves the reader with a direct final judgment."}]}
